node.title: High-multiplier three-petal LS6 atoms are guarded Pade quotient cells
node.statement: For one LS6 atom in the high-multiplier range e=deg(Etilde)>s=ell-a, every candidate has a unique quotient Q of degree e-a with fixed leading coefficient and is exactly D=quo_E(MQ), V=-rem_E(MQ), subject to deg(V)<=s, D|L_C, and gcd(D,Q)=1. If F is the canonical inverse of E modulo M, then D=rem_M(FV); on the official a<=ell/2 branch, nonemptiness forces deg(F)>=ell+a. Thus the high range is a two-sided guarded Pade/rational-approximation cell rather than an unstructured BC flat. This is a coordinate reduction, not a split-divisor payment.
